name: milestone-tracker
title: Milestone tracker
description: Milestones of a P6 project against its baseline: dates, variance in working and calendar days, float and critical flags, the open milestones most late and what drives the first one (the database is never written). Use when the user asks about milestones, key dates or how the milestones compare with the baseline.

args.name: project
args.description: Project ID as shown in P6

args.name: baseline
args.description: Project ID of the baseline to compare with (empty: the project baseline set in P6)

template:
Milestone tracker of project {project}: every milestone with its date, baseline date, variance, float and critical flag, the open milestones most late against the baseline and what drives the first one. Nothing is written to the database.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules and checks to run before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order. Each call is one page: the report shows that page and says when there are more,
so do not read further pages.
1. ms = p6_milestones(project="{project}", baseline="{baseline}", limit=30): every milestone by date with its baseline date and variance, counts, baseline, must finish date.
2. late = p6_milestones(project="{project}", baseline="{baseline}", open_only=true, order="variance", limit=10): open milestones, largest variance in working days first.
3. drv = p6_driving_path(project="{project}", target=<late.rows.0.task_code>, limit=15): driving predecessors of the open milestone with the largest variance. <late.rows.0.task_code> is the field rows.0.task_code of the result of late: when it is null or missing, skip this call (its fields are null).
Leave out an argument whose value is empty (baseline).

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

For this skill:
- The variance of a milestone is its own field: never work it out from two dates.

# Milestone tracker of {project}

Data date {data_date}, last schedule run (F9) {last_f9}. Each milestone has one date: the start of a start milestone, the finish of a finish milestone, actual else forecast (early date of the last F9). Variance = date minus baseline date: positive = later than the baseline.

[if: stale]
Warning: this project was changed after its last F9. Dates, float and critical flags are out of date until it is rescheduled in P6 (F9).
[end if]

[if not: baseline_project]
No baseline: this project has no project baseline and none was given, so no milestone has a baseline date or a variance. Set a project baseline in P6, or give the Project ID of a baseline.
[end if]

## Summary

- Baseline: {baseline_project} (baseline dates: {baseline_dates}).
- Must finish by: {must_finish}.
- Milestones: {n_milestones}; completed: {n_completed}; open: {n_open}, of which critical: {n_critical} ({critical_definition}).
- Against the baseline: late {n_late}, of which open {n_open_late}; early {n_early}; on time {n_on_time}; without a baseline date {n_no_baseline}.

[if: n_open_late]
Warning: {n_open_late} open milestones are forecast later than their baseline date.
[end if]

## All milestones, by date

[table: all]

## Open milestones, largest variance first

[table: late]

[if: target_code]
## What drives {target_code} - {target_name}

This is the open milestone with the largest variance; its total float is {target_tf} d. Its driving predecessors on the early dates of the last F9 (level 0 is the milestone; completed activities are left out):

[table: drivers]

Each driving chain starts from:

[table: roots]
[end if]

[if not: target_code]
There is no open milestone, so there is no driving path to show.
[end if]

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- A call says the project is not found: "Project <project> was not found: check the Project ID (p6_list_projects)."
- A call says the baseline is not found: "Baseline <baseline> was not found: check its Project ID (p6_list_projects)."
- p6_milestones says the project has no data date or is an EPS node: repeat its message and stop.

## Warnings (fixed sentences of report.md)

- schedule_state.stale is true: keep the warning that the project changed after its last F9.
- baseline.project is null: keep the "No baseline" sentence; the variance columns then read n/a.
- counts.open_late is not 0: keep the warning on open milestones later than their baseline date.

## Cross-checks (each pair must be equal)

1. ms.schedule_state.data_date = late.schedule_state.data_date (same data date).
2. ms.schedule_state.data_date = drv.data_date (skip when drv was skipped).
3. ms.must_finish = late.must_finish.
4. ms.counts.open = late.counts.milestones.
5. ms.counts.open_late = late.counts.late.
6. ms.counts.critical = late.counts.critical.
7. late.rows.0.total_float_d = drv.target.total_float_d (skip when drv was skipped).

If a pair differs, the database changed between the calls: run the three calls again once. If it still
differs, say which pair differs and do not publish the figures it concerns.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you.
- Variances are the variance_wd (working days of the milestone's calendar) and variance_cd (calendar
  days) fields, never a difference of two dates you worked out.
- The tables keep the rows in the order returned and stop at their cap (all milestones 30, open
  milestones 10, drivers 15, chain starts 10). A table whose call has more pages (next_offset not null)
  ends with its line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> ...", both numbers copied from that call.
- Every milestone and activity is written "Activity ID - name".
- The driving path section is kept only when drv ran (target_code not null).
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names and number formats exactly as
  formatted.

# Fields of Milestone tracker

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. ms = p6_milestones(project="{project}", baseline="{baseline}", limit=30): every milestone by date with its baseline date and variance, counts, baseline, must finish date.
2. late = p6_milestones(project="{project}", baseline="{baseline}", open_only=true, order="variance", limit=10): open milestones, largest variance in working days first.
3. drv = p6_driving_path(project="{project}", target=<late.rows.0.task_code>, limit=15): driving predecessors of the open milestone with the largest variance. <late.rows.0.task_code> is the field rows.0.task_code of the result of late: when it is null or missing, skip this call (its fields are null).
Leave out an argument whose value is empty (baseline).

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.

## Arguments

- {project}: Project ID as shown in P6, as given
- {baseline}: Project ID of the baseline to compare with (empty: the project baseline set in P6), as given

## Units

- wd: working days of each activity's calendar
- cd: calendar days
- d: days of each activity's calendar (hours / hours per day)
- count: a count

## Slots

| Slot | Field (call.path) | Unit | Format | None | Meaning |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| data_date | ms.schedule_state.data_date |  | date | n/a | data date of the project |
| last_f9 | ms.schedule_state.last_schedule_date |  | datetime | n/a | last schedule run (F9) in P6 |
| stale | ms.schedule_state.stale |  | flag | n/a | this server changed the project after the last F9 |
| baseline_project | ms.baseline.project |  | text | none | Project ID of the baseline compared with (null: no baseline) |
| baseline_dates | ms.baseline.dates |  | text | n/a | baseline date rule: current = the baseline's actual else forecast date |
| must_finish | ms.must_finish |  | date | n/a | project must finish by date (PROJECT.plan_end_date) |
| critical_definition | ms.critical_definition |  | text | n/a | the project's definition of critical |
| n_milestones | ms.counts.milestones | count | int | n/a | milestones of the project (start and finish milestones) |
| n_completed | ms.counts.completed | count | int | n/a | completed milestones |
| n_open | ms.counts.open | count | int | n/a | milestones not completed |
| n_critical | ms.counts.critical | count | int | n/a | open milestones that are critical |
| n_late | ms.counts.late | count | int | n/a | milestones later than their baseline date |
| n_early | ms.counts.early | count | int | n/a | milestones earlier than their baseline date |
| n_on_time | ms.counts.on_time | count | int | n/a | milestones on their baseline date (within 5 minutes of working time) |
| n_no_baseline | ms.counts.no_baseline | count | int | n/a | milestones without a baseline date |
| n_open_late | ms.counts.open_late | count | int | n/a | open milestones later than their baseline date |
| target_code | drv.target.task_code |  | text | n/a | Activity ID of the open milestone with the largest variance (null: no open milestone) |
| target_name | drv.target.task_name |  | text | n/a | its name |
| target_tf | drv.target.total_float_d | d | n1 | n/a | its total float |

## Table all

Every milestone by date then Activity ID.

Rows: ms.rows, in the order returned, at most 30.
When ms.next_offset is not null, add the line: Showing the first <returned> of <total> milestones. (returned and total of ms).
No rows: write 'This project has no milestone.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Milestone | task_code + task_name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Type | task_type |  | text | n/a |  |
| Status | status_code |  | text | n/a |  |
| Date | date |  | date | n/a |  |
| Date kind | date_kind |  | text | n/a |  |
| Baseline date | baseline_date |  | date | n/a |  |
| Variance (wd) | variance_wd | wd | n1 | n/a |  |
| Variance (cd) | variance_cd | cd | n1 | n/a |  |
| Vs baseline | vs_baseline |  | text | n/a |  |
| Total float (d) | total_float_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Critical | critical |  | flag | n/a |  |

## Table late

Open milestones, largest variance in working days first, without a baseline date last, then by date.

Rows: late.rows, in the order returned, at most 10.
When late.next_offset is not null, add the line: Showing the first <returned> of <total> open milestones. (returned and total of late).
No rows: write 'No open milestone.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Milestone | task_code + task_name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Forecast | date |  | date | n/a |  |
| Baseline date | baseline_date |  | date | n/a |  |
| Variance (wd) | variance_wd | wd | n1 | n/a |  |
| Variance (cd) | variance_cd | cd | n1 | n/a |  |
| Vs baseline | vs_baseline |  | text | n/a |  |
| Total float (d) | total_float_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Critical | critical |  | flag | n/a |  |

## Table drivers

The milestone (level 0) and its open driving predecessors, by level then early finish.

Rows: drv.rows, in the order returned, at most 15.
When drv.next_offset is not null, add the line: Showing the first <returned> of <total> activities. (returned and total of drv).
No rows: write 'No driving predecessor.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Level | level |  | int | n/a |  |
| Activity | task_code + task_name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Status | status_code |  | text | n/a |  |
| Early start | early_start |  | date | n/a |  |
| Early finish | early_finish |  | date | n/a |  |
| Total float (d) | total_float_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |
| Drives | successor + successor_name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Link | type |  | text | n/a |  |
| Lag (d) | lag_d | d | n1 | n/a |  |

## Table roots

What starts each driving chain: data_date, constraint, actual_date (progress), open_start (no predecessor), completed_predecessor, unexplained.

Rows: drv.drivers_at_root, in the order returned, at most 10 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 10 items, add the line: Only the first 10 chain starts are shown.
No rows: write 'No chain start found.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Activity | task_code + task_name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Starts from | type |  | text | n/a |  |
| Date | date |  | date | n/a |  |

## Cross-checks (equal values)

- same data date in both milestone calls: ms.schedule_state.data_date = late.schedule_state.data_date
- same data date in the milestones and the driving path: ms.schedule_state.data_date = drv.data_date
- same must finish date in both milestone calls: ms.must_finish = late.must_finish
- open milestones = milestones of the open list: ms.counts.open = late.counts.milestones
- open late milestones = late milestones of the open list: ms.counts.open_late = late.counts.late
- same critical milestones in both calls: ms.counts.critical = late.counts.critical
- same total float of the first open milestone: late.rows.0.total_float_d = drv.target.total_float_d

# Milestone tracker of DEMO-SS225

## Summary

- Baseline: DEMO-SS225_BL (baseline dates: current).
- Must finish by: 2027-08-16.
- Milestones: 11; completed: 3; open: 8, of which critical: 7 (project setting CT_TotFloat: total float <= 0 h (critical_drtn_hr_cnt); open activities).
